summary: Iter159 — verification of the WALL-CLOCK guard fix in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/stories/viewer/[userId].tsx. Static + regression tests confirm: (1) storyStartTsRef = useRef(Date.now()) declared (line 175), (2) wall-clock branch inside setProgress computes elapsed = Date.now() - storyStartTsRef.current and, if elapsed < STORY_DURATION_MS - TICK_MS, returns 1 (caps visually) WITHOUT triggering advance (lines 605-610), (3) storyStartTsRef.current is reset in useEffect[idx] (line 671) AND in a separate useEffect[currentUserId] (line 679) to cover the jumpToUser case where target idx equals current idx. All iter155-158 protections intact (advanceLockRef, transform:scaleX, unique key `${currentUserId}-${i}`, jumpToUserRef proxy, imageLoadedRef inline sync, single clearInterval in cleanup). Backend regression 4/4 PASS (feed, stories/user, view invalid id, anonymous auth). Frontend smoke: home renders without red screen. 9/9 pytest checks green.
critical_code_review_comments: Wall-clock guard implementation VERIFIED via regex assertions on the source file. Key invariant: even if `next = p + INCREMENT >= 1` is reached prematurely (image cache-hit onLoad firing instantly, tick catch-up after JS backlog, batched setState burst), the callback checks `Date.now() - storyStartTsRef.current < STORY_DURATION_MS - TICK_MS` and returns 1 (visual cap) WITHOUT calling setIdx. Next tick re-evaluates. Guarantees ~7s wall-clock per story regardless of upstream races.

Two independent effects reset the timestamp: `useEffect [idx]` handles same-user next/prev; `useEffect [currentUserId]` handles jumpToUser atomic swap when target idx == previous idx (React would skip [idx] effect due to Object.is equality). Belt-and-braces confirmed.

Progress bar visual correctness: `pct` is computed from `progress` state which is capped at 1 by the wall-clock branch. `transform: [{ scaleX: pct }]` (line 853, transformOrigin: 'left center') means the bar fills smoothly left-to-right and stays at 100% when capped — no visible flashing to 1 and back.

No regression risk of the story lasting MORE than 7s: the guard only PREVENTS early advance; it does not delay it. Once `elapsed >= STORY_DURATION_MS - TICK_MS` the next tick that sees `next >= 1` proceeds normally (either advance to next idx or jumpToUser('next') at end-of-chain). Worst case additional delay = TICK_MS (50ms), imperceptible.
Backend endpoints unchanged and green: /api/stories/feed 200, /api/stories/user/{uid} 200, /api/stories/{invalid}/view returns 4xx (400/404/422), /api/auth/anonymous 200.
